assessments.reasoning: The Reference starts the default mode in move and updates it as a non-reference pattern implicitly dereferences the scrutinee. The explicit modifier rule and rejected 2024 examples impose the condition at the binding. The pinned 1.85 Edition Guide reproduces the earlier allowance and illustrates the fully explicit and implicit forms.

challenge.method: Follow shared and mutable implicit reference descent, check all three rejected 2024 examples and the earlier-edition note, and compare the Edition Guide's explicit replacement. Keep the neighboring restriction on reference patterns distinct.
challenge.results: The condition is the default mode at a particular binding, rather than an initial setting for every binding or a ban on all explicit modifiers. The adjacent & and &mut reference-pattern rule has separate scope. The edition is Rust 2024 even though the Reference source revision and Edition Guide distribution use separate identifiers.

limitations: This gives a necessary condition for writing those explicit modifiers, without asserting that every binding in default move mode satisfies all other type and borrowing constraints.
